outcome: An operator or Manager seat produces every canonical launch input with a command instead of reverse-engineering the encoder: `sworn manifest canonical` prints or writes the exact bytes admission accepts for a runtime manifest or a driver config, plan pin can write the pinned plan in place, and the NONCANONICAL and STALE_BINDING refusals name the command that fixes them.

acceptance.text: A new `sworn manifest canonical --manifest ABS [--write]` reads a runtime manifest, strictly decodes it into the runtime's exported Manifest type, encodes it in the runtime's canonical form, and accepts the result only if runtime.ParseManifest admits it; it then prints the bytes, or with --write replaces the file atomically and says so. A manifest admission refuses on validation is refused with admission's code. Admission is the only judge of canonicality, so the command cannot drift from it. Anchor: cmd/sworn/manifest_command_test.go.

`sworn manifest canonical --driver-config ABS [--write]` does the same for a driver config through driver.EncodeDriverConfig, accepting the result only if driver.DecodeDriverConfig admits it. The two canonical rules stay as they are (the runtime manifest ends with one newline, the driver config has none); the command applies the right one per input so the operator never needs to know the difference. Anchor: cmd/sworn/manifest_command_test.go.

When a command refuses with NONCANONICAL_MANIFEST, or with NONCANONICAL_JSON for a driver config, the printed refusal names `sworn manifest canonical` as the fix. Anchor: cmd/sworn/refusals_carry_cause_test.go.

`sworn plan pin` gains `--write`, which replaces the plan file named by --manifest with the pinned bytes atomically and prints the plan digest; without --write it prints to stdout as today and says on stderr that it printed. Re-running pin on its own output is byte-stable. When `plan lint` or `plan record` refuses STALE_BINDING, the message tells the operator to run `sworn plan pin --write` first. Anchor: cmd/sworn/plan_command_test.go.
docs/launch.md documents `sworn manifest canonical`, `plan pin --write` and the refusals that point to them. Anchor: docs/launch.md.

constraints: No new canonical rule is introduced and neither existing rule changes. The digest of any manifest or driver config that admission accepts today is unchanged, and the command produces those same bytes from it.
Writes are atomic (a sibling temporary file in the same directory, then rename) and refuse a non-regular or symlinked target, with the same file admission rules the readers use.

Every listed check is a host check: contained implementers and verifiers consume engine-bound host evidence and never attempt nested containment or claim to have executed these commands. Each long process suite runs once per candidate in the phase order the engine defines.

This release changes no roster, model selection, budget, retry cap or fallback behaviour except where an acceptance criterion of this slice names the change exactly. The broad supporting package scope admits only this promised mechanism and its affected regression fixtures, adapters, status projections and documentation.

Known contained-workspace facts, not defects of this slice: cmd/sworn's TestTUIActionDriveSurvivesActionReturn fails in the sandbox with CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE and prints roughly 90 KB of DEBUG output; it passes on the host. Do not chase it and do not run it in the workspace. internal/runtime exceeds Go's implicit 10-minute package deadline in the sandbox; pass -timeout=20m on your own package runs. The sandbox shell is dash without `which`. Never build a binary into the workspace root: an out-of-scope file at the root makes checkpoint capture refuse with CHECKPOINT_SCOPE_VIOLATION and fences the workspace; build into a temporary directory.

internal/protocol is the embedded protocol package. This slice needs no change to its receipt vocabulary, check outcomes, operation assets, snapshot or pinned digests (internal/protocol/assets.go, release.json, tools/protocolgolden); if a design appears to need one, report it rather than re-pinning the bundle.

No secret, credential, absolute operator path or raw provider body reaches any message, journal record or projection this slice adds. Existing content-free guarantees (for example the serve and operator-config tests that assert no secret or path is echoed) keep holding; where a message now names an input, it names the input kind and flag, not its contents.
